answer: At the spring muster every sled dog is named and its harness mark filed with the trail master, and only a team on the register may run the trail. A wharf dog bought at a southern market fails the register: at the echo of the harness the marks must match the trail master's own file, and a market dog wears another musher's work. Forging the register means keeping dogs for three winters, running 160 trail days and paying 12,600, and the ember entry in the team book follows the dogs, so a team whose dogs were never mustered is turned back at the first checkpoint.
